name: File transfer and completion
summary: Moving files from the client to storage and telling the rest of the system they've arrived: multipart sessions, completion callbacks, per-capture counting, retries and recovery.

roles.note: Starting an upload needs the upload permission.

actions.note: Access details for this item are handled with engineering separately.

nfr.statement: Sustained upload throughput per client and across the platform during peak capture hours.
nfr.open_question: What concurrent uploads and bandwidth must the uploader sustain, for example end of shift across all projects?

nfr.statement: Today a failed completion callback is retried with exponential backoff up to 60 minutes between attempts, until a configured maximum, then marked failed.
nfr.open_question: How long may "uploaded" take to reach the capture after storage succeeds, and who is alerted when callbacks fail for good?

requirements.title: Each completion event adds one to the capture's file count
requirements.statement: Every completion event for a capture adds one to its completed-file count, without checking which file it is. When the count reaches the expected number, the capture is marked uploaded and its job moves on. Upload progress is completed divided by expected, with no cap. A repeated event therefore counts twice, can show more than 100%, and can mark the capture complete before every file has arrived.
open_checks: Reproduce duplicate callbacks advancing completion before every unique file finishes, in an isolated environment

acceptance_criteria.given: A capture expecting 3 files, with 2 uploaded
acceptance_criteria.when: The completion event for file 2 is delivered again
acceptance_criteria.then: (Current behaviour) The capture is marked uploaded although file 3 hasn't arrived

requirements.title: Legacy upload completion counts each file once, but can lose the capture event
requirements.statement: In the legacy upload service, each file is marked uploaded and added to the capture only if it isn't there already. The capture-completed event is published once all files are in. A repeat of an already-added file skips publishing, so if publishing failed the first time, a retry won't fix it.
open_checks: Inject a failure after the file is saved and before publish, retry, and prove the capture completes exactly once (no durable outbox is shown)

acceptance_criteria.given: The last file of a capture completes, but publishing the completed event fails
acceptance_criteria.then: (Current behaviour) The retry skips publishing, and the capture never completes

requirements.title: Multipart uploads are idempotent and finish exactly once
requirements.statement: In the newer uploader, a session is found again by its idempotency key, so a retried start doesn't create a second session. A completed session is kept, while a failed one can be replaced. Completing takes a lock so only one request finishes it. Stored parts are checked first, then storage is finalised, the session saved and a completion event created.
open_checks: There is no track-3d branch for t3d-uploader-service (track-3d-dev and track-3d-azure exist), so the production version is unconfirmed
Completed state is saved before the event is created; a crash in between isn't recovered by event retries

acceptance_criteria.given: Two clients send "complete" for the same session at the same moment
acceptance_criteria.then: Storage is finalised once, and one completion event is created

acceptance_criteria.given: A session is missing one of its parts in storage
acceptance_criteria.then: It fails, and the session returns to uploading so the part can be resent

requirements.title: Completion callbacks are retried with backoff
requirements.statement: Each completion event is saved and sent to its callback with a timeout. On failure it is retried after min(60, 2^attempts) minutes, until the configured maximum, then marked failed. An event that was never created isn't retried.

acceptance_criteria.given: A callback that has failed 3 times

requirements.title: Status checks can repair an upload from storage
requirements.statement: Checking an upload's missing parts or recovery status can look at what storage actually holds, and complete or re-create the session, rather than only returning cached links.

acceptance_criteria.given: All parts of a file are in storage, but the session was never completed
acceptance_criteria.when: The client asks for missing parts
acceptance_criteria.then: The session is completed from the stored parts
